source: Complete pipeline for manipulating wide-format COVID-19 pandemic data in R.

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load Data
confirmed <- read_csv("corona_confirmed.csv")
recovered <- read_csv("corona_recovered.csv")
deaths    <- read_csv("corona_deaths.csv")

# 2. Snapshot Calculations on March 22nd
total_cases <- confirmed %>% select(`3/22/20`) %>% sum()
total_cases_north_of_equator <- confirmed %>% filter(Lat > 0) %>% select(`3/22/20`) %>% sum()
total_australia_cases <- confirmed %>% filter(`Country/Region` == 'Australia') %>% select(`3/22/20`) %>% sum()

cat("Total Global Cases:", total_cases, "\n")
cat("Northern Hemisphere %:", total_cases_north_of_equator / total_cases * 100, "\n")
cat("Australia %:", total_australia_cases / total_cases * 100, "\n")

# 3. Group and Summarize Data
countries_confirmed <- confirmed %>% group_by(`Country/Region`) %>% summarize_at(vars(-Lat, -Long, -`Province/State`), sum)
countries_recovered <- recovered %>% group_by(`Country/Region`) %>% summarize_at(vars(-Lat, -Long, -`Province/State`), sum)

# Max-value recovery rate for US
max_confirmed_us <- countries_confirmed %>% filter(`Country/Region` == 'US') %>% select(-`Country/Region`) %>% max()
max_recovered_us <- countries_recovered %>% filter(`Country/Region` == 'US') %>% select(-`Country/Region`) %>% max()
cat("US Max Recovery Rate %:", max_recovered_us / max_confirmed_us * 100, "\n")

# 4. Transpose and Clean
transposed_confirmed <- countries_confirmed %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  row_to_names(row_number = 1)

transposed_confirmed <- apply(transposed_confirmed, 2, as.numeric) %>% as.data.frame()

# 5. Visualize Growth Curve
transposed_confirmed <- transposed_confirmed %>% mutate(date = 1:nrow(transposed_confirmed))

ggplot(transposed_confirmed, aes(x = date, y = Italy)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
  labs(x = "Days Since Jan 22, 2020", y = "Confirmed Cases", title = "COVID-19 Trajectory in Italy") +
  theme_minimal()
